deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 150v is the blank back of a printed Bremen freight form ('Frachtzettel für die Fahrpost', No. 13). The ruled columns are headed 'No. der Karte | Zeichen | Stück | [blank] | Pfund | Loth'. The recto's print (No. 13, 'Frachtzettel für die Fahrpost auf den Cours von BREMEN nach') shows through mirror-reversed. Faint mirrored handwriting also shows through in the middle of the sheet; it is not legible as text on this side.

The only writing on the page is a two-line title at the top, in a hand that may not be Riemann's (possibly a later archivist or editor): 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen / von B. Riemann'. There is also a short pencil or ink mark in the 'Stück' column, possibly a tally or check mark, or a numeral such as '7'. The sheet therefore works as a wrapper or cover leaf for the following folios.

Those folios hold a draft of the introduction to Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle's Journal 54, 1857). The draft discusses determining a function of x+yi on a surface T from prescribed discontinuities. It writes w = u+vi with u_xx + u_yy = 0, obtained by eliminating v from the Cauchy–Riemann equations i ∂w/∂x = ∂w/∂y. It refers to a related idea of Gauss, which is the Dirichlet principle setting. None of this derivation appears on 150v itself.
